test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 15 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Article 17 of the Indian Constitution enforces the :

options.text: joint sitting of both houses in certain cases
abolition of the practice of untouchability

solution:
The correct answer is __**abolition of the practice of untouchability**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 17 of the Indian Constitution explicitly abolishes "untouchability" and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• It mandates that the enforcement of any disability arising out of "untouchability" shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.
 
• The Article is a fundamental right and is enforceable in the courts of law.
 
• Article 17 is part of the Right to Equality, which spans Articles 14 to 18 in the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Education**

 
 
• Article 21A of the Indian Constitution mandates free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• This was added by the 86th Amendment Act in 2002.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion**
 
 
• Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution guarantee freedom of religion to all citizens.
 
• These articles provide the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
 
 
• **Joint Sitting of Both Houses in Certain Cases**
 
 
• Article 108 of the Indian Constitution provides for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament to resolve a deadlock on a bill.
 
• This is convened by the President of India.
